name: ZCA_ES_FAILURES
description: This table is used to store the hierarchy snapshots

columns.name: FAILURE_ID
columns.description: the primary key, which is the id of the failure

columns.name: BATCH_ID
columns.description: the batch id processed by the ess_request_id, null if dynamic batch processing is disabled

columns.name: ESS_REQUEST_ID
columns.description: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the request ID of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: META_MODEL_VERSION_UUID
columns.description: the uuid of the meta model that this snapshot was created for

columns.name: ENTITY_UUID
columns.description: the uuid of the entity the failure is for

columns.name: DOCUMENT_ID
columns.description: the id of the document where failure occured

columns.name: HTTP_STATUS
columns.description: the HTTP status of the failure, if any

columns.name: FAILURE_TYPE
columns.description: the failure type reported by Elastic Search

columns.name: REASON
columns.description: the rason fo rthe failure as reported by Elastic Search

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: USER_LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Disconnected Mobile: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row. This value is different from LAST_UPDATE_DATE if the update originally happened in a different database (i.e. a different mobile database or the server).
